name: Mistica Foods — Runge Street

hero.alt: Renovated production room at Mistica Foods with insulated metal panel walls and ceiling, ceiling-mounted refrigeration units, and insulated high-speed roll-up doors

overview: Wright Construction Management served as design-build construction manager for the comprehensive renovation and expansion of Mistica Foods' 123,000 square-foot food processing facility in Franklin Park, Illinois, with a final construction cost of $22.3 million.
The project transformed the facility's production and cold storage environments, supporting Mistica Foods' operational growth in the highly regulated food and beverage sector.

blocks.heading: Scope of Work
paragraphs: The scope covered a full interior renovation. New insulated metal panel (IMP) wall and ceiling systems were installed throughout, along with extensive underground plumbing including trench and floor drain systems.

Mechanical and electrical work included a new boiler and thermo-fluid heating system and significant refrigeration system upgrades. Structural concrete work encompassed both new floor slabs and exterior improvements, and a new primary electrical service was installed to support expanded operations.

blocks.alt: Interior of the plant stripped to subgrade during demolition, with the existing structural steel columns and roof deck exposed
blocks.caption: Interior demolition opened the floor to subgrade for new underground plumbing, trench drains, and floor slabs.

items.alt: Insulated metal panel wall and ceiling installation underway, with scissor lifts and stacked panels staged across the production floor
New boiler and thermo-fluid heating equipment installed inside the Mistica Foods facility

blocks.heading: Working Around Live Production
paragraphs: WCM coordinated more than ten specialized trade contractors while the plant maintained partial operations — a complex logistical challenge in an active food processing environment.
Sequencing the work so production could continue drove how the interior was staged, how trades were released, and how each area was turned back over to the owner.

blocks.alt: Production floor in operation with conveyor lines, packing stations, and product crates in a renovated area of the plant
blocks.caption: Portions of the plant stayed in production while adjacent areas were under construction.

items.alt: New primary electrical service equipment installed along an interior wall of the facility
Rooftop mechanical units and piping runs installed on the roof of the Mistica Foods facility

blocks.heading: Phasing and Permitting
paragraphs: Cold storage construction and food processing facility construction both carry demands that a general renovation does not. WCM managed the phased work and the rigorous permitting process with the Village of Franklin Park.

blocks.alt: Pallet racking installed in the renovated cold storage area, with insulated metal panel walls and an evaporator at the far end
blocks.caption: Renovated cold storage, racked and ready for turnover.

blocks.heading: What Made It Demanding
paragraphs: Technical complexity, occupied-facility constraints, and the integration of advanced building systems defined this project. It reflects WCM's capacity to deliver large-scale, technically demanding industrial work while minimizing operational disruption for food and beverage clients.
